en.title: Minimum Total Distance with Two Warehouses
en.description:
Choose any two warehouse positions on the number line; each center goes to its nearer warehouse, and the sum of all centers' distances should be minimized. The warehouses may coincide, and neither is required to serve any center.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n values dist_centers. The original gives no value ranges; this site sets 1≤n≤200000, −10⁹≤position≤10⁹.
en.explanation: Example 1: put the warehouses at 1 and 10, for a total distance of 0+1+0+1=2. Example 2: put a warehouse at 7, for a total distance of 0. Example 3: either both ends, or one endpoint together with 5, gives the minimum total distance 5.
hints: After sorting, the service areas of the two warehouses are split by one cut into two contiguous parts. A single part is optimal at its median; use prefix sums to compute a part's distance in O(1), and enumerate every cut.
